Une flûte, un tambour, des mains qui fra: A flute, a drum, clapping hands. It was the first evening the island danced.
Quelques signes gravés pour qu'un air su: A few carved signs so that a tune outlives whoever sings it. The island lullaby finally passes from one family to another.
Une corde, puis sa moitié, puis ses deux: A string, then its half, then its two thirds: he tunes his instruments by ear and by ruler. The island's lyres sound together.
Chaque cloche de bronze donne deux notes: Each bronze bell gives two notes depending on where it is struck. The square's carillon comes from here.
On y étudie la musique comme les nombres: Music is studied here like numbers, without touching an instrument. Musicians find it strange, and send their children.
Des notes sur des lignes, et une chanson: Notes on lines, and a song nobody has ever heard is sung right first time. The choir learns ten times faster.
Chacun chante une ligne différente, et l: Everyone sings a different line, and the whole stands up. On rehearsal nights, the windows on the square stay open.
Fanfare en majeur le dimanche, complaint: A brass band in major on Sundays, a lament in minor on rainy evenings. Passing musicians bring other scales.
On y imprime les partitions, portée par: Scores are printed here, staff by staff. A tune written here is played on the mainland the following month.
Il triche un peu sur chaque note pour qu: He cheats a little on every note so that they all get along. The island harpsichord finally plays in every key.
Du théâtre où l'on chante au lieu de par: Theatre where people sing instead of speaking. The premiere played to a full house, and the stands had to be enlarged.
On y empile les notes par trois et on ap: Notes are stacked in threes here and you learn which follow one another. The island's songs have gained a proper ending.
Ses murs ont été calculés pour que le de: Its walls were calculated so that the back row hears like the front. First, sand was made to dance on a plate.
Un pendule qui bat la mesure, une fourch: A pendulum that beats time, a steel fork that gives the A. The orchestra starts together, for once.
Chaque tuyau ajoute sa couleur à la même: Each pipe adds its own colour to the same note. He knows why a flute does not sound like an oboe, and he plays on it.
Une voix gravée dans la cire, qu'on rééc: A voice engraved in wax, which you can listen to again whenever you like. The island's grandmothers have left their songs there.
On y joue ce qui n'a ni tonique ni refra: Music with neither tonic nor chorus is played here. Half the audience whistles, the other half comes back the next week.
Un instrument qu'on joue sans le toucher: An instrument you play without touching it, another full of cables. The power station keeps a little current for them on Saturday nights.
On y mesure ce qu'on entend encore, et o: They measure what you can still hear, and explain why a tune gives you shivers. The blacksmiths leave with earplugs.
Chaque son y est découpé en nombres et g: Every sound is cut into numbers here and kept without wearing out. Everything the island has ever sung fits in one cupboard.
